title: The Last Static Anew
premise: Mara Oyelaran keeps the beacon on derelict relay station Kestrel-9, a job so obscure it may have been invented to hide him. When a distress signal arrives in extinct Ashanti-Spacer creole, he traces it to Vessel Yard, where two hundred miners were supposedly relocated—not massacred—according to every official record. As Mara digs, he discovers the beacon itself was built to jam the truth, and its original commissioner was his own grandmother, who died trying to broadcast the massacre. Pursued by Concordance enforcers and aided by Iyo, a defector archivist he comes to love against every duty he has, Mara must rebuild the beacon into a transmitter and force the galaxy to remember. In the end he broadcasts the truth at the cost of the station and nearly his life, justice arriving outside any courtroom, while Iyo carries the surviving records into exile.
about_author: Vesper Whitlock is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to frequencies nobody else claimed. They write science fiction about people entrusted with small, strange responsibilities that turn out to hold up the world.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Establishes his solitary routine maintaining the beacon aboard Kestrel-9: calibration logs, ration runs, conversations with an AI that barely speaks. He insists he chose this invisibility. Emotional beat: contentment with a hairline crack of loneliness beneath it.

chapters.title: A Language With No Speakers
chapters.summary: Mara intercepts a distress fragment in Ashanti-Spacer creole, extinct for two centuries. His grandmother's lullabies are the only reason he can parse it. POV Mara. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into unease—who could be sending this?

chapters.title: Kestrel's False Heart
chapters.summary: Mara discovers the beacon emits a low-level jamming field aimed at a coordinates cluster near Vessel Yard. The AI admits the order predates both of them. POV Mara. Emotional beat: the floor of his identity tilting.

chapters.title: The Archivist Who Defected
chapters.summary: Iyo Senn arrives unannounced, claiming to be a records auditor; her forged credentials fool everything but Mara's instinct. POV alternating Mara/Iyo. Emotional beat: mutual suspicion sharpened by reluctant fascination.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Souls, Relocated
chapters.summary: Official files say the Vessel Yard miners were 'relocated with full compensation.' Iyo shows him the compensation ledger: every signature identical. POV Iyo. Emotional beat: cold horror dressed in bureaucratic calm.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Buried
chapters.summary: In the beacon's foundation code, Mara finds encrypted layers signed with his grandmother's name—the beacon was her hiding place for evidence of the massacre. POV Mara. Emotional beat: grief and betrayal braided together.

chapters.title: The Concordance Comes Calling
chapters.summary: An enforcer vessel requests 'routine inspection.' Mara plays the dull caretaker while Iyo hides in the jamming shadow. POV Mara. Emotional beat: terror performed as boredom.

chapters.title: Ashes at Vessel Yard
chapters.summary: They reach the yard's hulk: scorch patterns, sealed vents, children's shoes fused to decking. The relocation ships never existed. POV Iyo. Emotional beat: proof turning witness into mourner.

chapters.title: Love Against Protocol
chapters.summary: Trapped in a decompression delay, Mara and Iyo speak honestly for the first time—her family helped write the cover-up; his helped bury it. POV alternating. Emotional beat: intimacy kindled precisely because both are traitors to their inheritances.

chapters.title: The Order to Forget
chapters.summary: Concordance directive recovered: the beacon's true commission was to erase, not transmit. Mara realizes his whole life was maintenance of a lie. POV Mara. Emotional beat: rage at being made an instrument.

chapters.title: Running Silent
chapters.summary: Fleeing enforcer patrols through debris fields, Iyo pilots, Mara decodes. A near-miss forces them to jettison the archive copy. POV Iyo. Emotional beat: fear teaching them what they're willing to lose.

chapters.title: The Witness in the Wreckage
chapters.summary: A survivor's black box surfaces: audio of the massacre's first hour. Listening to it breaks something open in both of them. POV Mara. Emotional beat: testimony as wound and weapon.

chapters.title: Bargaining With Ghosts
chapters.summary: They seek a retired Concordance judge living in disgrace, hoping she'll authenticate the evidence. She agrees—for a price: they leave her out of the broadcast. POV Iyo. Emotional beat: the bitter arithmetic of allies.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Fuel Depot
chapters.summary: The judge's aide sells their location. Enforcers board; Iyo is captured covering Mara's escape with the black box. POV Mara. Emotional beat: guilt as engine.

chapters.title: Interrogation of the Archivist
chapters.summary: Iyo's POV under detention. She feeds her interrogators a false trail while memorizing their chain of command—the same officers who signed the relocation order. Emotional beat: defiance refined into patience.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Beacon
chapters.summary: Mara returns to Kestrel-9 and reverses his grandmother's work: converting the jammer into a transmitter powerful enough to reach every inhabited system. POV Mara. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed as purpose.

chapters.title: The Rescue That Shouldn't Work
chapters.summary: Using the false trail Iyo planted, Mara infiltrates the detention barge and pulls her out mid-transfer. POV alternating. Emotional beat: love declared in gunfire, quietly.

chapters.title: Countdown to Silence
chapters.summary: Enforcer fleet inbound; the transmitter needs ninety minutes they don't have. Iyo proposes broadcasting from inside the blast radius. POV Iyo. Emotional beat: resolve without bravado.

chapters.title: The Last Static
chapters.summary: Climax. Under fire, Mara keys the transmission: the black box audio, the ledgers, the names of two hundred dead read aloud in their own language. The station takes direct hits. POV Mara. Emotional beat: triumph and annihilation in the same breath.

chapters.title: What the Galaxy Heard
chapters.summary: Aftermath across colonies: riots, resignations, tribunals the Concordance can't suppress. The judge breaks her bargain and testifies anyway. POV Iyo. Emotional beat: justice arriving untidily, outside the law.

chapters.title: Salvage
chapters.summary: Mara, burned and half-deaf, is pulled from the wreck by salvage crews who recognized the broadcast. He learns his grandmother's final log message was addressed to whoever kept the light. POV Mara. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into belonging.

chapters.title: A New Commission
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Mara and Iyo, exiled but not erased, establish an independent archive-station broadcasting suppressed records. The last line echoes the creole lullaby: we remember so you cannot unmake us. POV alternating. Emotional beat: love and duty reconciled at last.
